newsitem.title: USA: Axel Springer to buy 10 percent of AOL Germany.
newsitem.headline: Axel Springer to buy 10 percent of AOL Germany.

text.p: AOL Europe, a joint venture of America Online Inc. and Bertelsmann AG, said Wednesday that Axel Springer Verlag, Germany's largest newspaper publisher, will buy a 10 percent stake in AOL Germany.

AOL Germany is the German subsidiary of AOL Europe. In exchange, AOL Europe gains access to some of the 40 newspapers and magazines Springer publishes in Germany, including Bild, a German language newspaper that has a circulation of about 5 million, the largest of all the daily newspapers in Europe.
A spokeswoman for Dulles, Va.-based America Online said the companies were not releasing any financial details.

Springer has equity stakes in more than 90 newspapers and magazines worldwide. It also holds a strong position in electronic media through its partnerships with four television stations and seven radio stations in Germany.
AOL said it will feature several Springer publications such as the German newspaper Bild, and its specialised publications, such as Auto Bild, Sport Bild and Computer Bild.
The companies plan joint direct marketing activities.
Separately, AOL said AOL Europe has passed 300,000 subscribers, with AOL Germany at nearly 200,000. Britain is approaching 100,000 and AOL France has about 25,000 members.

Since early November, when America Online posted a $353.7 million fiscal first quarter loss due to accounting charges, AOL stock has almost doubled, roaring with the bull market and amid Wall Street's optimism about the actions AOL has taken to remain an industry leader.
On Nov. 7, AOL closed at $24.75. On Wednesday, AOL rose $2.625 to $40.125 amid optimism about the performance of the world's largest online service.

At a Jupiter Communications conference in New York on Tuesday, the president of AOL Services, Ted Leonsis, said November was the best month ever for AOL in terms of advertising and usage. He declined to give specifics.
"All I can say is, it was a great month," Leonsis said.
In the past two weeks, some Wall Street analysts have become more bullish on the stock, with Cowen & Co. upgrading stock to a buy rating, with a 12-month price target of $55.
